name: legesher-vscode
description: Write Python code in your native language with real-time translation

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace, the legesher.serverCommand setting is not read from workspace settings: it names an executable the extension spawns, so only your user-level value (or the bundled default) is used until you trust the workspace.

legesher.targetLanguage.description: Deprecated: use legesher.workingLanguage instead. Honoured as an alias while workingLanguage is not set.
legesher.targetLanguage.markdownDescription:
The language **you** read and write code in.

This is your own preference — it changes what you see, not what the repository stores, so people on the same project can each work in their own language.

The vocabulary every translation routes through is `#legesher.sourceLanguage#`; each file is stored in the language its author wrote it in.
legesher.targetLanguage.markdownDeprecationMessage: Deprecated: use `#legesher.workingLanguage#` instead. This setting is still honoured as an alias whenever `#legesher.workingLanguage#` is not set, so existing configurations keep working — but new configurations should set the new name.

legesher.workingLanguage.description: The language you read and write code in right now
legesher.workingLanguage.markdownDescription:
The language **you** read and write code in right now — your *working language*.

This is your own preference — it changes what you see, not what the repository stores, so people on the same project can each work in their own language. A file written in a different language keeps its own *file language*; this setting decides what the UI renders for you.

Replaces the deprecated `#legesher.targetLanguage#`, which is still honoured while this setting is not set. The languages you read comfortably are `#legesher.knownLanguages#`; the vocabulary every translation routes through is `#legesher.sourceLanguage#`, and each file is stored in the language its author wrote it in.

legesher.knownLanguages.description: The languages you read comfortably. Seeded from your working language when empty.
legesher.knownLanguages.markdownDescription:
The languages you read comfortably — your *known languages*, as ISO 639-1 codes (for example `["pt", "en"]`).

The language picker lists these first, and files already written in one of them raise no language-mismatch signal: opening a Farsi file is only noteworthy if you do not read Farsi.

When empty, the set is seeded from `#legesher.workingLanguage#`, so the language you work in always counts as known. Edit it with the **Legesher: Manage My Languages** command.

legesher.sourceLanguage.description: The vocabulary every translation routes through: Python's own (en)
legesher.sourceLanguage.markdownDescription:
The vocabulary every translation routes through: Python's own, `en`. Not what the repository stores: each file is stored in the language its author wrote it in, and this setting only names the pivot.

To change the language *you* read code in, use `#legesher.workingLanguage#`.

**Note:** Only English (`en`) is currently supported.

enumDescriptions: Infer each file's language from its contents, falling back to the configured language when the file gives no clear signal.
Always use the configured language. Set automatically when you pick a language explicitly.
legesher.languageDetection.description: Whether to detect a file's language from its contents. Folder and workspace settings always take precedence over detection.

legesher.serverCommand.description: Command that starts the Legesher language server. The default, legesher-lsp, is installed by the legesher-language-server Python package. Hover, completion, diagnostics and keyword highlighting need it.

legesher.trace.server.description: Traces communication between VS Code and the language server

legesher.enabled.description: Enable or disable the Legesher extension

legesher.telemetry.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable usage telemetry to help improve Legesher. Off by default; also gated by VS Code's global telemetry setting. Events contain **no code content, no file paths, and no identifiers we collect**; the bundled VS Code telemetry library adds a pseudonymous machine id.

legesher.telemetry.repoAttribution.markdownDescription:
Consent to opt-in usage attribution: a repository label attached to requests to Legesher's hosted service.

**This setting records your choice only.** The extension does not send this label today, and no request is gated on this setting. It exists so your choice is on record before any such request ships; if that changes it will be announced in the changelog and in the extension README first.

The label is not secret. It is a SHA-256 hash of the repository's normalized `origin` remote URL with no key, so anyone who knows a remote URL can compute its label and tell whether that repository is in use. A repository with no remote gets a label salted per install instead. Requires `#legesher.telemetry.enabled#` and VS Code's own telemetry setting.

legesher.telemetry.contributeToMLTrainin.markdownDescription:
Consent to contribute translation feedback towards improving Legesher's translations.

**This setting records your answer only.** Legesher does not currently send translation corrections, and no telemetry event is gated on this setting. It exists so your consent is on record before any such event ships; if that changes it will be announced in the changelog and in the extension README first.

Legesher never collects your code, file paths, or personal information. You can change this anytime. [Learn more about our privacy practices](https://docs.legesher.io/privacy#ml-training)

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Legesher
walkthroughs.description: Code in your native language with full Python IDE support

steps.title: Welcome to Legesher 🌍
steps.description:
Legesher enables you to code Python in your native language.💻 We currently support 51 languages (like Arabic, Hindi, Portuguese) with plans to expand to new languages and dialects. The possibilities are endless when technology speaks your language. 

Explore and innovate freely! Your code stays in your language in git, and the form Python executes is produced only when the code runs.

steps.title: Install the Full Legesher Suite
steps.description:
This extension provides **visual feedback** - syntax highlighting, hover translations, and the translation panel.

To actually **write and run code** in your native language, you'll need the full Legesher package suite. Follow the installation instructions to get started.

[View Installation Instructions](https://github.com/legesher/preview-repo/blob/main/docs/INSTALLATION.md)

steps.title: Choose Your Target Language
steps.description:
Select a natural language you want to code in. You can change this anytime.

[Select Language](command:legesher.selectLanguage)

steps.title: View Translations Side-by-Side
steps.description:
See your code translated in real-time with a side-by-side panel. Click below to open a sample Python file with the translation panel.

[Try It Now](command:legesher.tryTranslationPanel)

steps.title: Hover for Translations
steps.description:
Hover over any Python keyword or builtin to see its translation in your target language and in the source language.

Try hovering over `def`, `print`, or `if` in any Python file!

steps.title: Help Us Improve
steps.description:
Found a translation that could be better? Let us know! Your feedback helps make Legesher more accurate for everyone.

[Give Feedback](command:legesher.giveFeedback)

scripts.pretest: npm run typecheck && npm run compile && npm run compile:integration && npm run lint && npm run test:unit
